House league → a season

The house league season page, before and after

This page has more of Stage 3 on it than any other: a card title set as a small label, Title Case buttons and window titles, and labels over each value. Both pictures are the live dev screen (UAT Rep Club, its 2026 Fall House League), in Warm, at true size. The proposed picture is the same page with the new lettering applied in the browser from the product’s own type settings. Nothing was saved.

Changes RESTYLED“DIVISIONS” becomes a section title, “Divisions”, in the normal font at 16 px (A3). The buttons read “Close registration”, “Add division”, “← All seasons”, and the window titles follow (“Edit season”, “Delete division”).
Stays UNCHANGEDThe small labels over each value (ACTIVE, PENDING, SEASON DATES, REGISTRATION FEE, STATUS) stay labels, as you ruled in A10. Their words become sentence case underneath, but they still show in capitals. The status chip stays a chip.

Accounting

Ledger → Starting and Ending balance rowsRESTYLED

The capitals also swallowed the date (“OCT 1, 2026”). Proposed: sentence case at the row’s current size and weight, so the date reads as a date. The design review suggested making these two labels larger than the rows between them. I kept the size: the Ledger is the product’s one dense register, every row at the same small size, and a larger label next to a small amount would split the row.

What the design review changed

The design review read these drawings against the product’s written rules before you saw them. Applied: help search’s group heads became band headings (they had come out the same as the labels inside them); card prices moved onto the size ladder; the notifications toggle now matches the drawer’s, and “Needs attention” changes in both; the first-run rows’ values came onto the ladder; the colour-code picture was re-taken so the change shows. Declined, with the reason in the captions: a larger Ledger balance label, and changing Stage 1’s “GUIDES” label on the help hub to match Rename web addresses. “GUIDES” heads the one set of cards on the hub, while “Active teams” splits one list into two groups, so they are different roles.

Your calls · Stage 3

Five calls

C1 and C2 are the two the build prompt raised; C2’s premise turned out to be wrong, and the ask says how. C3 and C4 came out of re-reading the words. C5 is the Stage 2 leftover. Each carries my recommendation. Pick, add a note if you like, then build the paste-back at the bottom. Nothing gets built until you rule.

C1 · The public-site editor

You ruled in A13 to fix the public-site editor in this stage, because Club Tier Stage 4 was still to come. Stage 4 was drawn on 19 October. Its drawings include the editor, and its last step (4c) rebuilds it with section controls. Its card titles (“PAGE CONTENT”, “SOCIAL LINKS”, “DISPLAY OPTIONS”) and five Title Case words would be redone by that rebuild, and a 4c session working in the same file at the same time would collide with this one.

Rides on it: 8 elements on one screen. Nothing else in Stage 3 depends on it.

C2 · Status words: one spelling across the product

The prompt worried that changing “Pending Review” in house league alone would create two spellings. There are already two. House league registrations, tournament results and the scorekeeper, a team’s status and the public status lookup say “Pending Review”. Rep-team tryouts, house league’s notifications and emails, and the printed tournament schedule say “Pending review”. “Registration Open / Closed” is split the same way: Title Case in house league and on the public league pages, “Registration open” wherever tournaments use it. Nothing stores or compares these words. The product stores a code and turns it into words for display, so a rename is safe.

Rides on it: about 60 lines of screens, help and tests for “Pending Review”, and 22 for “Registration Open / Closed”. The tests that pin the words change with them. “Waitlisted” is one word and needs nothing.

C3 · A screen’s name inside a button

The list wanted “Open Families”, “Go to Overview”, “Open Allocations” and “Loading the Venue library…” in sentence case. Each one names a screen as the menu names it, and that is already the shipped pattern: the Budget vs. Actual screen says “Open the Budget”, “Open the Ledger”, “Open Coming due”, and a build check holds those words. Lowering only these four would make two rules.

Rides on it: 4 elements stay as they are under the first option. The second reopens the money screens shipped on 18 October.

C4 · Four wrong things found while reading the words

These are not capitals. Each one tells the customer something untrue. (1) Plan & billing says to use “Manage Subscription below”, but no button has that name; the real one is “Payment method & invoices”. (2) First-run setup ends on “Go to Dashboard”; there is no Dashboard, the club’s hub is Overview. (3) PDF settings says “Upload a logo in Org Settings”; the page is called Settings. (4) A rep team’s past season lists every staff member who is not the head coach as “Assistant Coach”, a team manager included. And one defect: (5) on a house league season’s Send notification page, choosing “Waitlist” or “Pending review” sends the email to nobody. The page asks for a status that does not exist, the server finds no one, and the page reports 0 sent without an error. Only “All active registrants” works.

Rides on it: /docs follows (1) and (3). Two lines go to /marketing without a call from you: first-run setup’s “Free League includes…” (not a plan name), and the League plan’s billing page offering “a full club outside your tournament” to a league.

C5 · The theme colour Stage 2’s capture saved by accident

In Stage 2 the capture helper clicked into an autosaving field and saved two colours on the dev tournament “uat-phase2c-plus-championship-2026”: primary #1E3A8A and accent #D9F99D. Both were empty before. This stage’s captures only navigated, scrolled and searched help, and saved nothing.

Rides on it: nothing in the build. It only changes how that dev tournament looks.
